ml-naive-bayes-07: Teen classes hain aur priors alag-alag ($0.5, 0.3, 0.2$). Sirf likelihood dekh ke $C_3$ ko jitaana galat hoga — prior bhi multiply hota hai.
Har class ka score $= P(c)\,P(x \mid c)$. Phir $P(C_3 \mid x) = \text{score}(C_3)/(\text{teeno scores ka sum})$.
Scores: $C_1 = 0.5 \times 0.2 = 0.10$, $C_2 = 0.3 \times 0.5 = 0.15$. Ab $C_3$ ka score aur total nikaalo. Trap: unnormalised score hi likh dena.
ml-naive-bayes-08: Likelihood $A$ ke favour mein hai ($0.6 > 0.2$), par prior $B$ ke favour mein ($0.8$). Decision dono ke product se hota hai.
Compare karo $P(A)P(x \mid A)$ vs $P(B)P(x \mid B)$. Denominator $P(x)$ dono mein same hai, toh cancel ho jaata hai.
$P(A)P(x \mid A) = 0.2 \times 0.6 = 0.12$. Ab $B$ ka product nikaalo aur dekho kaunsa bada hai. Trap: sirf likelihood compare karna.
ml-naive-bayes-09: Neg class mein $F_1$ kabhi present nahi hua (0 of 6) — bina smoothing ke Neg ka score zero ho jaata. Isliye Laplace yahan zaroori hai.
Binary feature: $P(F = v \mid c) = (\text{count} + 1)/(N_c + 2)$. Score $= P(c) \cdot P(F_1{=}1 \mid c) \cdot P(F_2{=}0 \mid c)$, priors $0.4$ aur $0.6$.
Neg: $P(F_1{=}1) = 1/8$, $P(F_2{=}0) = (3+1)/8 = 4/8$. Ab Pos ke dono smoothed values ($N = 4$, denominator 6) nikaalo. Trap: denominator mein sirf $+1$.
ml-naive-bayes-10: Multinomial model hai aur document mein *cheap* do baar aaya hai — har occurrence alag factor deta hai. Spam mein *meeting* ka count zero hai, par smoothing on hai.
$P(w \mid c) = (\text{count} + 1)/(8 + 4)$. Score $\propto P(\textit{cheap} \mid c)^2 \cdot P(\textit{meeting} \mid c)$; equal priors cancel.
Spam: cheap $= 5/12$, meeting $= 1/12$. Ab ham ke smoothed values likho aur dono scores compare karo. Trap: *cheap* ko ek hi baar ginna.
ml-naive-bayes-11: Char alag claims: class-independent factor, evidence $P(x)$, generative vs discriminative, aur assumption ka sach hona. Har ek ko Bayes rule se judge karo.
$P(c \mid x) = P(c)\prod_j P(x_j \mid c) / P(x)$. Jo factor har class mein same ho, wo normalise karte waqt cancel hota hai.
Option 2: agar $P(x_j{=}v \mid c)$ sab classes ke liye equal hai toh har score same number se multiply hua — ratio badla? NB $P(x \mid y)$ model karta hai ya $P(y \mid x)$?
ml-naive-bayes-12: "Independent" parameters gino: jo numbers baaki se nikal aate hain (jaise $1 - p$), wo free nahi hain.
Prior: 2 classes ⇒ 1 free number. Har class aur har binary feature ke liye sirf $P(x_j{=}1 \mid c)$ free hai, kyunki $P(x_j{=}0 \mid c) = 1 - P(x_j{=}1 \mid c)$.
Feature parameters $=$ (classes) $\times$ (features) $= 2 \times 10$. Ab prior wala add karo. Trap: $P(x_j{=}0)$ ko alag ginna, ya full joint table ginna.
ml-naive-bayes-13: Variances alag hain (1 aur 4), toh Gaussian density ka front factor $1/\sigma$ bhi matter karega, sirf exponent nahi.
$p(x \mid c) = \frac{1}{\sigma\sqrt{2\pi}}e^{-(x-\mu)^2/(2\sigma^2)}$. $A$: $\sigma = 1$, $\mu = 2$; $B$: $\sigma = 2$, $\mu = 5$. Equal priors, toh densities ka ratio hi posterior ratio hai.
$A$ ka exponent: $-(3-2)^2/2 = -0.5$. $B$ ka exponent $-(3-5)^2/8$ — ye bhi nikaalo, phir $1/\sigma$ factors compare karo. Trap: exponent mein $\sigma$ use karna, $\sigma^2$ nahi.
ml-naive-bayes-14: Model Bernoulli hai: har word ek alag binary feature (present/absent). Vocabulary size 50 yahan denominator mein nahi aata.
Laplace binary feature ke liye: $(\text{count} + 1)/(N_c + 2)$, kyunki do outcomes hain. Yahan count $= 0$, $N_c = 8$.
Numerator $0 + 1 = 1$. Ab denominator $8 + (\text{outcomes ki sankhya})$ likho. Trap: multinomial wala $+V$ ya sirf $+1$ lagana.
ml-naive-bayes-15: "Prediction galat hone ki probability" $= 1 - \max$ posterior. Pehle teeno posteriors chahiye, priors ke saath.
Score$(c) = P(c)P(x \mid c)$; posterior $=$ score / sum. Error $= 1 - \max_c P(c \mid x)$.
Scores: $C_1 = 0.2 \times 0.5 = 0.10$, $C_2 = 0.3 \times 0.4 = 0.12$. $C_3$ ka score aur total nikaalo. Trap: max posterior ko hi error bol dena.
ml-naive-bayes-16: Char claims: log-scores, $\alpha \to \infty$ smoothing, smoothing kab decision badalta hai, aur NB ka parameter count. Har ek ko formula se check karo.
Add-$\alpha$: $P(w \mid c) = (n_w + \alpha)/(N_c + \alpha V)$. NB: $P(x \mid c) = \prod_j P(x_j \mid c)$ — har feature ki apni chhoti table.
Option 2 test karo: counts $1/1$ vs $5/10$ (bina smoothing), aur $V = 10$ ke saath $(1+1)/(1+10)$ vs $(5+1)/(10+10)$ — kaunsa bada hai?
ml-lda-06: Fisher direction sirf mean difference nahi hai — $S_W$ ka inverse bhi lagta hai. Yahan $S_W$ diagonal hai, toh inverse aasaan hai.
$w \propto S_W^{-1}(\mu_1 - \mu_2)$, aur $S_W^{-1} = \operatorname{diag}(1/2, 1)$. Phir $w$ ko itna scale karo ki pehla component 1 ho.
Pehla component: $4/2 = 2$. Doosra component nikaalo, phir dono ko 2 se divide karo. Trap: $S_W$ se multiply kar dena, ya seedha $(4, -2)$ lena.
ml-lda-07: Covariances alag hain ($I$ aur $4I$) — LDA ki shared-covariance condition yahan nahi hai. Boundary ka shape quadratic terms se tay hoga.
$\ln p_1 - \ln p_2$ mein $-\frac12\lVert x - \mu_1\rVert^2$ aur $+\frac18\lVert x - \mu_2\rVert^2$ aate hain. Check karo $\lVert x\rVert^2$ cancel hota hai ya nahi.
$\lVert x\rVert^2$ ka coefficient $-\frac12 + \frac18$ — zero hai kya? Agar nahi, aur dono covariances $I$ ke multiple hain, toh $a\lVert x\rVert^2 + (\text{linear}) = \text{const}$ kaunsa curve hai?
ml-lda-08: Variance same (9), par prior class 2 ka bada (0.8). Threshold midpoint 7 se hatega — class 2 ka region badhna chahiye.
$\ln(0.2/0.8) = \ln 0.25 \approx -1.386$ aur $\mu_2 - \mu_1 = -6$. Ab shift $9 \times (-1.386)/(-6)$ nikaalo aur 7 mein jodo. Trap: $\sigma = 3$ use karna.
ml-lda-09: Mean difference $(2, 2)$ hai, par $S_W$ diagonal nahi — $x_1$ direction mein spread zyada hai. Fisher direction mean difference se tilt hogi.
$w \propto S_W^{-1}(\mu_1 - \mu_2)$. 2×2 inverse: $\frac{1}{ad - bc}\begin{pmatrix} d & -b \\ -c & a \end{pmatrix}$, yahan $\det = 4 \cdot 2 - 2 \cdot 2 = 4$.
$S_W^{-1} = \frac14\begin{pmatrix} 2 & -2 \\ -2 & 4 \end{pmatrix}$. Ab isse $(2, 2)$ multiply karo aur options se match karo. Trap: $S_W$ se multiply karna.
ml-lda-10: "Maximum value of $J$" poocha hai, direction nahi. Pehle optimal $w$ nikaalo, phir $J$ mein daalo.
Optimal $w = S_W^{-1}d$. Plug karne par $J_{\max} = d^\top S_W^{-1} d$ ban jaata hai. Yahan $S_W^{-1} = \operatorname{diag}(1/2, 1)$, $d = (3, 1)$.
$w = (3/2, 1)$. Ab $w^\top d$ aur $w^\top S_W w$ nikaalo, phir $(w^\top d)^2 / (w^\top S_W w)$. Trap: $w = d$ hi daal dena, ya numerator square na karna.
ml-lda-11: LDA ke directions ki limit classes ki ginti se aati hai, features (10) se nahi — PCA aur LDA ka yahi farak hai.
Between-class scatter $S_B = \sum_k n_k(\mu_k - \mu)(\mu_k - \mu)^\top$. Iska rank $\le K - 1$, kyunki deviations ka weighted sum zero hai.
Yahan $K = 4$ classes, $d = 10$ features. Directions $\le \min(K - 1, d)$ — ab number nikaalo. Trap: $K$ ya $d - 1$ likh dena.
ml-lda-12: Char claims: QDA ka variance, Gaussian NB ka LDA se rishta, priors ka boundary pe asar, aur unit change. Har ek ko "kitne covariance parameters" se socho.
LDA: sab classes ka ek $\Sigma$ (boundary linear). QDA: har class ka alag $\Sigma_k$. Prior sirf constant $\ln(\pi_1/\pi_2)$ jodta hai.
Option 4: $x' = Ax$ karo, toh $\mu' = A\mu$ aur $\Sigma' = A\Sigma A^\top$. Mahalanobis distance $(x' - \mu')^\top\Sigma'^{-1}(x' - \mu')$ badla ya wahi raha?
ml-lda-13: Within-class scatter mein har class apne khud ke mean se deviation leti hai, overall mean se nahi. Sirf second feature ($x_2$) chahiye.
$(S_W)_{22} = \sum_{A}(x_2 - \bar x_{2,A})^2 + \sum_{B}(x_2 - \bar x_{2,B})^2$. Average nahi lena, sirf sum.
Class $A$ ke $x_2$: 2, 4, mean 3, deviations $-1, +1$. Ab class $B$ ke $x_2$ values 1, 1, 4 ka mean aur squared deviations nikaalo. Trap: overall mean use karna.
ml-lda-14: Prior badalne se 1-D LDA mein kya hilta hai — threshold ki position, ya boundary ka shape? Aur kis taraf?
$\pi_1 = 0.7$: $\ln(0.7/0.3) > 0$ aur $\mu_2 - \mu_1 > 0$, toh shift ka sign kya hai? $d$-D formula mein prior $w$ mein aata hai ya sirf $b$ mein?
ml-lda-15: Shared $\Sigma = I$, toh boundary line hai; par priors unequal (0.75 vs 0.25), toh line perpendicular bisector se khiskegi.
Equal scores: $-\frac12\lVert x\rVert^2 + \ln 0.75 = -\frac12\lVert x - \mu_2\rVert^2 + \ln 0.25$. $\lVert x\rVert^2$ cancel karke linear equation banao.
Expand karke milta hai $2x_1 + 2x_2 = 4 + \ln 3$. Ab 2 se divide karo aur $x_2 = 0$ rakho. Trap: $\ln 3$ ko 2 se divide karna bhool jaana.
ml-lda-16: PCA labels nahi dekhta — sabse zyada total spread wali direction. LDA labels dekhta hai — wo direction jahan classes alag hon aur andar ka spread kam ho.
Total scatter ke diagonal entries ($x_1$ aur $x_2$ ke liye) compare karo PCA ke liye. LDA ke liye $w \propto S_W^{-1}(\mu_A - \mu_B)$.
Overall mean $(0, 0)$; $x_1$ values sab $\pm 4$ hain. Class means $(0, 1)$ aur $(0, -1)$ — mean difference kis axis pe hai? Ab $x_2$ ka total scatter bhi nikaalo.
ml-svm-margin-07: Margin width poocha hai — dono margin hyperplanes ke beech ki doori. Ye sirf $w$ pe depend karta hai, $b$ pe nahi. Dhyan do: yahan 3-D hai.
Width $= 2/\lVert w\rVert$ with Euclidean norm $\lVert w\rVert = \sqrt{w_1^2 + w_2^2 + w_3^2}$.
$\lVert w\rVert = \sqrt{1 + 4 + 4}$ nikaalo, phir 2 ko usse divide karo. Trap: $1/\lVert w\rVert$ (half-width) ya $2/\lVert w\rVert^2$ likhna.
ml-svm-margin-08: Do cheezein chahiye: distance (magnitude) aur point boundary ke kis side hai (sign of $f$).
Distance $= |w^\top x + b|/\lVert w\rVert$, yahan $w = (1, -2)$, $b = 3$. Side $= \operatorname{sign} f(x)$.
$f(1, 4) = 1 - 2(4) + 3$ — iska sign dekho. $\lVert w\rVert = \sqrt{1^2 + 2^2}$. Trap: $\lVert w\rVert^2$ ya $|w_1| + |w_2|$ se divide karna.
ml-svm-margin-09: Sirf do training points — dono support vectors hain, aur $w$ unke difference ke parallel hoga. Par $w$ ka scale $f(x_\pm) = \pm 1$ se fix hota hai.
$w = c(x_+ - x_-) = c(2, 2)$. Do equations: $w^\top x_+ + b = 1$ aur $w^\top x_- + b = -1$.
$x_- = (1, -1)$ pe $w^\top x_- = c(2 - 2) = 0$, toh $b = -1$. Ab $x_+$ wali equation se $c$ nikaalo, phir $f(5, 2)$. Trap: $c = 1$ maan lena.
ml-svm-margin-10: Jo point margin ke bahar hai (non-support vector), uska constraint inactive hai — use hataane se solution nahi badalta.
Har point ke liye $y\,f(x)$ nikaalo with $f = x_1 - 2$. $y f = 1$ ⇒ support vector; $y f > 1$ ⇒ margin ke bahar.
$(3, 0)$: $y f = 3 - 2 = 1$. $(1, 1)$: $y f = -(1 - 2) = 1$. Ab $(3, 2)$ aur $(0, 3)$ ke values nikaalo. Trap: sochna ki ek SV hata do toh doosra SV kaafi hai.
ml-svm-margin-11: Har statement ko "constraint $y_i f(x_i) \ge 1$ active hai ya nahi" se judge karo. Margin width ka formula bhi yaad karo.
Naya point jiska $y f > 1$ — purana $(w, b)$ feasible rehta hai. Jiska $y f < 1$ — purana $(w, b)$ constraint todta hai. Width $= 2/\lVert w\rVert$.
Option 1: kya $2/\lVert w\rVert$ mein support vectors ki ginti aati hai? Option 2: boundary dono margin lines ke beech kahan hoti hai?
ml-svm-margin-12: Ye trained SVM nahi hai, bas ek classifier. Geometric margin = sabse paas wale point ki signed distance, isliye min $y_i f(x_i)$ chahiye.
Har point ke liye $y_i f(x_i)$ with $f = 2x_1 + x_2 - 4$, minimum lo, phir $\lVert w\rVert = \sqrt{2^2 + 1^2}$ se divide karo.
A: $y f = 2(3) + 2 - 4 = 4$. C: $y f = -(2 - 4) = 2$. Ab B aur D nikaalo aur minimum chuno. Trap: $\lVert w\rVert$ se divide karna bhoolna.
ml-svm-margin-13: Teen cheezein dekho: objective min hai ya max, constraint mein label $y_i$ hai ya nahi, aur right-hand side 1 hai ya 0.
Margin width $= 2/\lVert w\rVert$; isse maximise karna $= \lVert w\rVert$ minimise karna. Scale fix karne ke liye support vectors pe $y_i f(x_i) = 1$.
RHS 0 wale option mein $w = 0$, $b = 0$ daal ke dekho — constraint satisfy hota hai? Aur $y_i$ hata do toh negative points ka kya hoga?
ml-svm-margin-14: Sirf do points — dono support vectors, aur margin width unke beech ki doori ke barabar hai. Poocha $\lVert w\rVert$ hai, width nahi.
Width $= \lVert x_+ - x_-\rVert = 2/\lVert w\rVert$. Yahan $x_+ - x_- = (3, 4)$.
$\lVert (3, 4)\rVert = \sqrt{9 + 16}$. Ab $2/\lVert w\rVert$ ko isse equal karke $\lVert w\rVert$ nikaalo. Trap: width ko hi $1/\lVert w\rVert$ maan lena.
ml-svm-margin-15: Har point ke liye $y\,f(x)$ nikaalo: $= 1$ margin pe, $0$ aur $1$ ke beech andar (sahi side), negative matlab galat side.
$f(x) = x_1 + x_2 - 3$. Inside margin ⇒ $0 < y f < 1$; on margin ⇒ $y f = 1$; misclassified ⇒ $y f < 0$. Sirf $|f|$ dekhna kaafi nahi.
ml-svm-margin-16: 1-D mein boundary sabse paas wale opposite points ke beech midpoint pe hoti hai. Par $(w, b)$ ka scale support vectors pe $y f = 1$ se fix hota hai.
Closest opposite pair: negative 1 aur positive 4. Equations: $w(4) + b = 1$ aur $w(1) + b = -1$.
Dono equations subtract karo: $3w = 2$. Ab $b$ nikaalo aur options se match karo. Trap: sirf boundary sahi hona kaafi nahi — $f(4) = 1$ bhi check karo.
ml-svm-soft-07: Label $-1$ hai par score positive ($0.3$) — point galat side pe hai. Hinge loss mein label ka sign zaroori hai.
Pehle $y f = (-1)(0.3)$ nikaalo, phir $1 - y f$. Trap: perceptron loss $\max(0, -yf)$ lena, ya $y$ bhool ke $1 - f$ likhna.
ml-svm-soft-08: Slack ki value se point ki position pata chalti hai: margin ke bahar, margin ke andar, ya galat side. Yahan $\xi = 0.4$ hai.
$\xi = 1 - y f$ jab $y f < 1$. Ranges: $\xi = 0$ ⇒ bahar/on margin; $0 < \xi < 1$ ⇒ andar, sahi side; $\xi > 1$ ⇒ misclassified.
$y f = 1 - 0.4$ nikaalo — positive hai ya negative, aur 1 se chhota ya bada? Trap: koi bhi $\xi > 0$ ko misclassified samajhna.
ml-svm-soft-09: Do candidates: P zero-slack par bada $w$, Q chhota $w$ par kuch slack. "Equal objective" ka matlab $C$ ke liye ek equation.
Objective $= \frac12 w^2 + C\sum\xi_i$, $\xi_i = \max(0, 1 - y_i f(x_i))$. Dono candidates ke liye $\frac12 w^2$ aur $\sum\xi$ alag nikaalo.
P: $\frac12(4^2) = 8$; check karo P ke saare $y f \ge 1$ hain. Q: $f = x - 2$ se $x = 1.5$ aur $x = 2$ ke slacks nikaalo. Trap: $f = 0$ wale point ka slack 0 maan lena.
ml-svm-soft-10: Table mein do symptoms: $C = 0.01$ pe dono errors high; $C = 1000$ pe train 0% par validation zyada. Ye bias aur variance ke classic signs hain.
Soft margin: $\frac12\lVert w\rVert^2 + C\sum\xi_i$. Chhota $C$ ⇒ slack sasta ⇒ wide margin; bada $C$ ⇒ slack mehenga ⇒ narrow margin.
Socho: high train + high validation error kaunsi problem hai, aur 0% train par 25% validation kaunsi? Trap: $C$ ki direction ulti samajhna.
ml-svm-soft-11: Hinge $\max(0, 1 - yf)$ ko $yf$ ke function ki tarah draw karo: kab zero hai, aur 0–1 loss se kahan alag hai?
$yf \ge 1$ ⇒ loss 0. $0 < yf < 1$ ⇒ point sahi side par loss $1 - yf$. 0–1 loss sirf $yf < 0$ pe 1 hota hai.
$yf = 0.5$ lo: hinge kitna, 0–1 loss kitna? Convexity ke liye: $\max$ of two affine functions convex hota hai ya nahi?
ml-svm-soft-12: Polynomial kernel: pehle dot product, phir 1 jodo, phir power 3. Order galat hua toh value badal jaati hai.
$x^\top z = 1 \cdot 4 + 2 \cdot (-1)$ nikaalo, phir $(1 + x^\top z)^3$. Trap: constant 1 bhool jaana, ya power 2 lagana.
ml-svm-soft-13: $(1 + x^\top z)^2$ ko expand karo — har alag term ek feature banti hai. Degree 0, 1 aur 2 teeno ke terms aate hain.
$(1 + x^\top z)^2 = 1 + 2\sum_i x_iz_i + \sum_i x_i^2z_i^2 + 2\sum_{i<j}x_ix_jz_iz_j$. Har group mein kitne terms hain, $d = 3$ ke liye?
Constant: 1 term. Linear $\sqrt2 x_i$: 3 terms. Ab squares aur cross terms ($i < j$ pairs) gino. Trap: $x_ix_j$ aur $x_jx_i$ ko alag ginna.
ml-svm-soft-14: $\gamma$ RBF kernel ki width control karta hai — slack penalty $C$ ka kaam hai, $\gamma$ ka nahi.
$K = e^{-\gamma\lVert x - z\rVert^2}$. Bada $\gamma$ ⇒ thodi si distance pe bhi $K$ bahut chhota. Chhota $\gamma$ ⇒ $K \approx 1$ door tak.
Distance 1 ke liye $\gamma = 100$ pe $K = e^{-100} \approx 0$. Toh har support vector ka asar kitni door tak jaayega? Trap: $\gamma \to 0$ aur $\gamma \to \infty$ ko ulta lena.
ml-svm-soft-15: Valid kernel ka Gram matrix do cheezein maangta hai: symmetric, aur positive semidefinite (koi negative eigenvalue nahi).
Symmetric 2×2 ke liye PSD ⇔ diagonal $\ge 0$ aur $\det \ge 0$. Pehle symmetry check karo, phir determinant.
Option 2: $\det = 1 \cdot 1 - 2 \cdot 2$. Option 4: $\det = 4 \cdot 1 - 2 \cdot 2$. Baaki do bhi check karo. Trap: singular ($\det = 0$) ko invalid samajhna.
ml-svm-soft-16: Kernel SVM ka $f(x)$ = support vectors ke kernel values ka weighted sum, label ke sign ke saath. Yahan $b = 0$ aur dono $\alpha = 1$.
$f(x) = (+1)K(s_1, x) + (-1)K(s_2, x)$, jahan $K(s, x) = e^{-\lVert s - x\rVert^2}$ (squared distance).
$\lVert x - s_1\rVert^2 = 0.25$, toh $K(s_1, x) = e^{-0.25} \approx 0.7788$. Ab $\lVert x - s_2\rVert^2$ aur $K(s_2, x)$ nikaalo. Trap: labels ignore karke dono jod dena.
